note: Lower model cost at equal answer quality. The launch demo -- and the reason quality is a GATE below, not a second goal: a cheaper colony that answers worse has not improved, it has been degraded.
Observe-only. It reports and never proposes: an error rate is a symptom, and a control loop that reacts to symptoms without a hypothesis is a random walk with receipts.

How often the curator of talky found a gap in what it could hand the brain, per hundred calls. Lower is better, and it is measured by the curator's own ledger rather than by a judge reading transcripts: a count the model did not produce is the only kind this loop may act on.

How often talky's brain had to read the same history again, per hundred calls. A high rate says the window handed over too little; the fix is a text slot (a tool description, a prompt block) and it only lands behind an evaluation batch.

Tool calls that came back with an error, per hundred calls. It is also talky's quality gate: talky's ledger has no rewrite advice to count, so a change that lowers another rate by raising this one has not improved anything.

How often the curator of cogny found a gap in what it could hand the brain, per hundred calls. Gated on `correction_rate`, because a thinner window that makes the thinking brain rewrite its standing advice more often is not a better window.
How often cogny's brain had to read the same history again, per hundred calls. Same gate as every cogny goal.

How often cogny's final answer rewrites a standing instruction (the `correction` key of its sidecar block), per hundred calls. It counts the model revising its own advice, NOT a person correcting the model -- the ledger has no deterministic signal for that -- and the name stays because the curator's mark is called that.
Tool calls of the thinking brain that came back with an error, per hundred calls.

How often cogny asks its requester a question back, per hundred calls. OBSERVE, never optimise: a question back is often the right answer, and a loop that drove this number down would teach the brain to guess.
